text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian newspapers this morning.

- Norwegians save more money in funds than in bank accounts, figures from the Central Bank show. Between April 1, 1996 and March 31 this year savings in funds rose by 1.6 billion crowns more than savings in bank accounts.

- The Bahamian-registred Hanseatic cruise liner ran aground in a fjord off the north coast of the Arctic island of Spitzbergen on Sunday with 260 passengers and crew on board. So far it is not known how the vessel run aground.

- More women than ever are choosing information technology (IT)-related courses. In the last two years the number of female students at the IT school in Baerum, outside Oslo, has increased by 200 percent. This autumn 30 percent of the school's new intake of 300 students will be women.

- Norwegian exports of seafood amounted to 11.2 billion crowns in the first six months of 1997, up 5.3 percent from the same year-ago period. Fifty-two percent of exports went to countries in the European Union.

- The fishing industry in Norway's most northerly county, Finnmark, has improved considerably. Four of the county's largest fishing companies improved operating results from 1995 to 1996 by a total of 35 million crowns.

- Large industrial companies such as metal producer Elkem and Norsk Hydro are threatening to move abroad if they are not ensured power supplies at low prices in Norway. Negotiations over new electricity contracts between industry and power producers are due to start soon.
